question: During the Later Vedic period, which of the following animals was specifically mentioned as useful for ploughing swampy land?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Buffalo**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• During the Later Vedic period, agricultural practices became more advanced, and specific animals were used for specialized tasks like ploughing land.
 
• The buffalo was particularly mentioned in texts as the preferred animal for ploughing swampy or marshy lands due to its strength and adaptability to wet conditions.
 
• Buffaloes were favored over cows or horses for such tasks because of their ability to navigate and work effectively in muddy terrains.
 
• References to buffaloes in agricultural contexts can be found in texts like the Satapatha Brahmana and other Later Vedic literature.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Later Vedic Period:**

 
 
• The Later Vedic period spans from approximately 1000 BCE to 600 BCE.
 
• This period saw advancements in agriculture, trade, and the use of iron tools.
 
• Texts such as the Satapatha Brahmana and the Taittiriya Brahmana provide insights into agricultural practices during this era.
 
 
 
• **Role of Animals in Agriculture:**
 
 
• Animals like buffaloes, cows, and oxen were integral to agricultural activities in ancient India.
 
• Buffaloes were specifically used for ploughing swampy or wet lands due to their ability to thrive in muddy conditions.
 
• Cows and oxen were more commonly used for regular ploughing and transportation.
 
 
 
• **Satapatha Brahmana:**
 
 
• The Satapatha Brahmana is one of the significant texts of the Later Vedic period.
 
• It provides detailed descriptions of rituals, agriculture, and the socio-economic practices of the time.
 
• References to buffaloes being used in agriculture highlight their importance in swampy land cultivation.
 
 
 
• **Iron Tools in Agriculture:**
 
 
• The use of iron tools during the Later Vedic period enhanced agricultural efficiency.
 
• Iron ploughshares were particularly effective in turning soil for cultivation.
 
• These tools complemented the use of animals like buffaloes in agricultural tasks.
